268288590_3e448aa3.text: A1 noradrenergic neurons in the medulla, A2 neurons in the nucleus tractus solitarius and A6 neurons in the LC project to many areas in the CNS, including the cortex, hippocampus, thalamus, and spinal cord 18 . The LC, a small nucleus located on either side of the fourth ventricle, contains the largest cluster of noradrenergic neurons in the CNS. LC neurons project to the cortex, hippocampus, amygdala, hypothalamus, cerebellum, and spinal cord 18 and modulate physiological processes, such as arousal, attention, cognition, anxiety, and responses to stress 18-21

268288590_ea7dcacc.text: We identified LC noradrenergic neurons in the pons by their location along the lateral margin of the fourth ventricle 28, 29 and by expression of tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) 26, a key enzyme involved in catecholamine synthesis. We also labeled LC neurons with anti-dopamine beta-hydroxylase (DBH) antibodies, an enzyme that converts dopamine to noradrenaline and is a marker of noradrenergic neurons 26, 30.
